verifications.claim: The NASA Artemis II rocket launched successfully on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R3: '6:35 pm ET April 1, 2026Artemis II liftoff!'; R5: 'NASA’s Artemis II SLS rocket lifted off from Kennedy Space Center at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R7: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, location, and successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) propelled four astronauts toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket making its first crewed launch'; R3: 'Artemis II SLS rocket'; R7: 'Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state SLS launched the four astronauts on the mission toward the Moon.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to travel around the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago' (1972/1973); R2: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R4: 'first time since 1972 during Apollo 17, human beings have left Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe it as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo in 1972.

verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II crew begins first day in space... orbiting the Earth'; R3: 'The crew is safely in orbit'; R4: 'Orion is on its way, bringing four humans towards the Moon... after leaving Earth orbit'; R7: 'The crew is now traveling at more than 15,000 miles per hour [in orbit]'
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch updates confirm crew entered Earth orbit before TLI.

verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Sources detail pre-launch issue with flight termination system, described as resolvable.
